title: Configurable data-sovereignty lifespans for interactive artifacts
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Goal:
Provide tenants and platform operators with first-class controls to declare per-tenant and per-route 'lifespans' (human-friendly retention intervals) for interactive artifacts (prompts, model responses, request logs, and derived metrics), with residency constraints and fully-automated evidence export bundles for compliance audits.

Scope:
- Surface a policy editor in Console that lets admins define: region residence requirement (e.g., EU-only), artifact type-specific lifespans, sampled vs full retention for metrics/logs, and automatic evidence export triggers (on legal-hold, periodic snapshot).
- Expose the same surface via API for infra-as-code flows.
- Implement server-side enforcement: per-request metadata evaluation, graceful fallback (if region unavailable), and attested export packaging.

Out of scope:
- Full encryption-at-rest redesign (we will integrate existing KMS flows).
- Cross-tenant aggregation analytics retention policies (future iteration).

Approach summary:
1) Policy model: introduce 'lifespan profiles' that bind: artifact_type -> retention_window (ISO duration), residency_constraint (region list or 'any'), sampling_policy (fraction or deterministic sampling rule), evidence_hook (none|on-eviction|periodic|legal-hold).
2) Enforcement: router attaches tenant profile id to requests; retention service records minimal index metadata and performs eviction according to window and sampling. Evictions generate a signed evidence manifest that can be exported.
3) Console UX: policy composer with validated presets (Safe, Balanced, Performance) and per-route overrides. Runtime simulator to preview expected storage and sampled exports for 30/90/365 day horizons.
4) API: tenant.policies.create/update/get/list endpoints and a retention-preview endpoint returning estimated bytes and sample counts.

Trade-offs and design decisions considered:
- Strict residency enforcement increases cross-region latency and reduces available capacity; chosen approach: default to a conservative residency-by-default preset for enterprise tenants and allow explicit opt-in to multi-region fallbacks with audit trail.
- Full fidelity logs vs sampled metrics: to keep cost predictable we will support deterministic reservoir sampling for metrics while keeping request logs intact for short horizons.

Success metrics:
- Self-serve tenant policy creation within Console without Sales assistance (success target: 95% of enterprise evals).
- 99% of evidence exports pass internal attestation checks and include per-eviction manifest.

Notes for engineering/ops:
- Must integrate with existing evidence-export pipeline (ENG-51234) and per-route retention proxy (ENG-99753) where available.
- Implement backfill and migration strategy to assign default lifespan profiles for existing tenants with opt-out window of 30 days.

acceptance_criteria: Console: Tenant admin can create a lifespan profile with artifact type rules, residency constraint, sampling policy, and evidence hook.
API: tenant.policies.create and tenant.policies.get return the persisted profile and validation errors for conflicting residency + evidence options.
Enforcement: New requests carry a policy-id; data is stored/evicted according to profile and eviction produces a signed evidence manifest.
Preview: Retention-preview API returns accurate estimated storage and sample counts within 10% of actual for 30-day simulated traffic for a provided tenant workload sample.
Export: Evidence bundles for 'on-eviction' and 'periodic' hooks are generated and accessible to tenant administrators for 90 days after creation.
Migration: Existing tenants receive a default Safe profile; opt-out window and audit log of changes exists and is testable in staging.
